attack_mechanism: The corresponding control/data route is `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.rf_rd -> neorv32_cpu_regfile.addr -> neorv32_cpu.rs1 -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr_wdata -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.rf_rd` reaches that selector or one of its CSR update controls; the implementation qualifies this propagation with `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.rf_wb_en`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.rf_zero`, `neorv32_cpu_regfile.addr`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.ir_funct3`, and the remaining path guards. The assignment `lsu_priv <= mstatus_mpp when mstatus_mprv = '1' else prv_level` makes `mstatus_mprv` the privilege-source selector. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.rf_rd` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.
